slides.title: After drought, Ethiopia braces for floods
slides.body: What El Niño could bring to the south and southeast

slides.title: Heavy rains expected from October
slides.body: FEWS NET expects above-average deyr/hageya rains, with heavy rain and flooding likely. FAO says flood risk rises October to December.

slides.title: people FAO aims to help
slides.body: Through a US$50 million appeal for June 2026 to March 2027, covering both drought and flood risks.

slides.title: woredas where early action was triggered
slides.body: By Ethiopia's Disaster Risk Management Commission. About 9.3 million people live there, FAO says.

slides.title: Flood-prone areas are on the list
slides.body: Southern Somali, South Ethiopia and South West Ethiopia, alongside drought areas of Afar, Amhara, northern Somali and Tigray.

slides.title: Rain alone won't end the crisis
slides.body: Herds are depleted and pasture is poor, so food access may improve only slowly, FEWS NET warns.

slides.title: Act early. Keep aid reaching every community.
slides.body: Follow for sourced updates from across Ethiopia.

source: Source: FAO & FEWS NET via Addis Standard · Aug 11 & Sept 15, 2026
